cross_product_finding: This statement is the clearest example in the batch of Capella's two-tier access model, which has no counterpart in server/. Layer 1 (management plane): execution is gated by a Capella organization/project role (Organization Owner, Project Owner, or Data Writer), checked by Capella's own control-plane authorization before the statement reaches the query engine. Layer 2 (data plane): 'cluster access credentials' (the database-user credentials analogous to server/'s classic RBAC users) are explicitly forbidden from running this statement at all - 'You cannot execute this statement using cluster access credentials.' server/ has only one layer: a cluster-admin-privileged user runs bucket-management operations (via REST/UI, not SQL++) and that single RBAC check is the whole story. Capella instead requires a distinct, non-database identity even to perform an operation that create/configures the database resource the RBAC system will later govern. This is a structural, not incidental, difference and likely needs its own relation shape (`requiresCapellaRole`) rather than forcing it into `requiresPrivilege`.
